papers.title_in_file: Leveraging Quantum Machine Learning Generalization to Significantly Speed-up Quantum Compilation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 2.2 (generalization bound), the algorithm description, hyperparameter discussion, benchmark conclusion and closing discussion; appendices skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A quantum compilation paper that uses a QML generalization-error bound to cut the cost of circuit instantiation in the BQSKit compiler.

assertions.value: The authors report that QF actor-Sample, incorporated in the BQSKit quantum compiler and compared against a state-of-the-art domain-specific optimizer, achieved an average speedup factor of 69 for circuits with more than 8 qubits.
quotes: we demonstrate improved scalability and a reduction in compile time, achieving an average speedup factor of 69 for circuits with more than 8 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that QF actor-Sample reduces the computational complexity of QF actor from O(4n) to O(M 2n), where n is the number of qubits and M is the number of states required for training, by making use of known bounds on the generalization error.
quotes: computational complexity from O(4n) to O(M 2n), where n is the number of qubits and M is the number of states required for training
assertions.certainty_reason: Complexity result argued in the paper and relying on a bound taken from other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that for circuits with fewer than five qubits it is better to use QF actor-RUST or CERES than QF actor-Sample.
quotes: if there are fewer than five qubits, it is better to use QF actor-RUST or CERES
assertions.certainty_reason: Guidance drawn from the paper's own benchmark set.

papers.title_in_file: Learning the tensor network model of a quantum state using a few single-qubit measurements
papers.what_it_is: A PAC-style protocol that learns a low-rank tensor network model of an unknown quantum state from single-qubit measurements, tested numerically.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical evidence of linear scaling, with the number of qubits, of the minimal size of the training dataset required to successfully predict the outcomes of future measurements.
quotes: We provide numerical evidence of linear scaling of the minimal size of the training dataset required to successfully predict the outcomes of future measurements with the number of qubits in the system.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from the paper's own simulations.

assertions.value: The authors score the learned model by R2 on an independent test dataset and use R2 = 0.5 as the threshold for adequate performance.
quotes: R2 is calculated using an independent test dataset.
We use the R2 = 0.5 value as a threshold indicating that the model reached adequate performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own evaluation setup, Fig. 4 discussion.

assertions.value: The authors report that the saturated R2 value drops for a larger number of qubits, which they associate with imperfect non-convex optimization of the loss function.
quotes: The saturated R2 value drops down in case of the larger number of qubits, which we associate with the imperfection of the non-convex multivariate optimization of the loss function with complex landscape.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation with an authors' attribution that is not tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that, compared to classical shadows and similar approaches, their algorithm uses only experimentally feasible single-qubit measurements and can be readily realized on existing experimental setups without additional overhead.
quotes: our algorithm uses only experimentally feasible single-qubit measurements and thus can be readily realized on the various existing experimental setups without any additional overhead
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim; the paper reports numerical tests only.

papers.title_in_file: Theoretical framework for quantum associative memories
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Preliminaries, storage-capacity statement, Section IX Discussion; Sections III to VIII and appendices skimmed by heading only
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that defines quantum associative memory through open quantum system dynamics (CPTP maps) and bounds its storage capacity.

assertions.value: The authors state that they derive a map that achieves an exponential increase in the number of stored patterns with respect to classical systems.
quotes: The map that achieves an exponential increase in the number of stored patterns with respect to classical systems is derived.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical derivation in the paper; no experiment; the Discussion words the advantage as potential.

assertions.value: The authors state that they develop a framework for quantum associative memory based on open quantum system dynamics, which lets them compare existing models, identify the theoretical prerequisites for associative memory tasks, and extend it in different forms.
quotes: we develop a comprehensive framework for a quantum associative memory based on open quantum system dynamics, which allows us to compare existing models, identify the theoretical prerequisites for performing associative memory tasks, and extend it in different forms
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Abstract and Introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that unitary-based quantum associative memories cannot exhibit fixed points of the dynamics, apart from the trivial identity case.
quotes: unitary-based QAMs cannot exhibit fixed points of the dynamics, with the exception of the trivial (identity) case
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Discussion as a consequence of the framework; no theorem number located.

assertions.value: The authors state that finding the best feature map for classifying classical input data is an open problem in quantum machine learning and beyond the scope of this work.
quotes: Of course, finding the best feature map is an open problem in the context of quantum machine learning and beyond the scope of this work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit, Section IX.

papers.title_in_file: A Review and Collection of Metrics and Benchmarks for Quantum Computers: definitions, methodologies and software
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Part I Introduction, the metric-template and general assumptions text of Part IV, and the Part V conclusion; the individual metric entries in Part IV and the hardware background in Part III were not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A National Physical Laboratory-led review and collection of quantum computer metrics and benchmarks, with methodologies, limitations and linked open-source software.

assertions.value: The authors state that the article provides a review of metrics and benchmarks for quantum computers, a comprehensive collection of benchmarks allowing holistic comparisons, a consistent format of definitions, and a reproducible approach linking the metrics to open-source software.
quotes: a comprehensive collection of benchmarks allowing holistic comparisons of quantum computers
a reproducible approach by linking the metrics to open-source software used to evaluate them
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that only a few metrics are widely used in practice, and that these typically include qubit relaxation and dephasing times or RB-based gate error metrics.
quotes: only a few metrics are widely used in practice
typically include the qubit relaxation and dephasing times
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement about the field; no survey of usage is shown.

assertions.value: The authors identify five areas where international standardization working groups could be established for quantum computer benchmarking.
quotes: We identify five areas where international standardization working groups could be established
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' recommendation, not a measured result.

assertions.value: The authors state that, although significant research has gone into metrics for gate-based quantum computers, much more limited research exists for non-gate-based devices such as quantum annealers, boson sampling devices, or analog quantum simulators.
quotes: although significant research has been devoted to developing metrics for gate-based quantum computers, much more limited research exists for non-gate-based devices such as quantum annealers, boson sampling devices, or analog quantum simulators
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' characterization of the literature.

papers.title_in_file: A Review of Barren Plateaus in Variational Quantum Computing
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2405.00781v2 dated 8 May 2025; the file name carries 2024-05 while the record id carries 2025. Same paper.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section II start, the classical simulability passage, Section X (classical vanishing gradients) and Section XI Implications and Outlook; Sections III to IX skimmed by heading only
papers.what_it_is: A review of the barren plateau phenomenon in variational quantum algorithms and QML models, its causes, mitigations and links to classical simulability.

assertions.value: The authors define a barren plateau as a state in which the parameter optimization landscape of a model becomes exponentially flat and featureless as the problem size increases.
quotes: When a model exhibits a BP, its parameter optimization landscape becomes exponentially flat and featureless as the problem size increases.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the term in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The review states that the presence of a barren plateau landscape implies that, for the overwhelming majority of parameter choices, an exponentially large number of measurement shots is needed to identify the loss minimizing direction.
quotes: the presence of a BP landscape implies that for the overwhelming majority of parameter choices an exponentially large number of measurement shots are needed to identify the loss minimizing direction
assertions.certainty_reason: Review statement of results from the cited literature.

assertions.value: The review states that many techniques that avoid barren plateaus encode the dynamics in a subspace that grows polynomially in the number of qubits, so that one should be able to simulate the information processing of the parameterized circuit and classically estimate the loss function.
assertions.anchor: Section IX, classical simulability of BP-free models
quotes: Since an exponentially large space is no longer being used, one should be able to simulate the information processing ability of the PQC, and thus classically estimate the loss function
assertions.certainty_reason: Review summary of cited work; the text itself notes the connection is an area of current analysis.

assertions.value: The authors state that the ultimate impact of the barren plateau phenomenon on the scalability of variational quantum models is still to be determined.
quotes: However, the ultimate impact of the BP phenomenon on the scalability of variational quantum models is still to be determined.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' view of the state of the field.

papers.title_in_file: Robust data encodings for quantum classifiers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, the existence-of-robust-encoding passage, the learnability and robustness tradeoff passage, and Section V Discussion and Conclusions; proofs in Section III and numerics in Section IV skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper that defines robust data encodings for binary quantum classifiers and proves robustness results under several noise channels.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for the common classifier they consider, they show that encodings determine the classes of learnable decision boundaries as well as the set of points that retain the same classification in the presence of noise.
quotes: For the common classifier we consider, we show that encodings determine the classes of learnable decision boundaries as well as the set of points which retain the same classification in the presence of noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proved in Section III A and III B per the Abstract and Section V; theorem numbers not checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that a robust encoding always exists for any trace preserving quantum operation, that the encoding may be trivial, and that this leads to a tradeoff between learnability and robustness.
assertions.anchor: Section III B and III D
quotes: by demonstrating there always exists a robust encoding for any trace preserving quantum operation. This encoding may be trivial, which leads to the idea of a tradeoff between learnability and robustness.
assertions.certainty_reason: Existence proof in Section III D, stated in Section III B; theorem number not checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that some of their analytical results help explain the finding in earlier literature that misclassifications due to depolarizing noise are solely due to finite shot statistics.
quotes: misclassifications due to depolarizing noise found in Ref. [35] are solely due to finite shot statistics
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' interpretation of a cited result.

assertions.value: The authors state that a clear task for future work is to test the ideas on a NISQ computer, because real devices show effects such as crosstalk that the channels they considered do not capture.
quotes: a clear task for future work is to test the ideas introduced here on a NISQ computer
more complicated effects such as crosstalk occur in real devices
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit, Section V.

papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2412.19336v2 dated 14 Nov 2025; the file name carries 2024 while the record id carries 2025. Same paper.

papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of modular quantum extreme reservoir computing for image classification, asking how few inter-module connections match a single reservoir.

assertions.value: The authors report that even a small number of well-placed connections between two modules can match single-reservoir accuracy, with simple one-to-one connections proving highly effective.
quotes: even a small number of well-placed connections between two modules can match single-reservoir accuracy, with simple one-to-one connections proving highly effective
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors report that performance generally improves with increasing inter-module entanglement, and that these correlations persist for both ZZ-coupled and random modular reservoirs.
quotes: Performance generally improves with increasing inter-module entanglement, and these correlations persist for both ZZ-coupled and random modular reservoirs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors report extensions to three modules and evaluations across MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, and state that their analysis uses simulations.
quotes: Extensions to three modules and evaluations across multiple datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10)
and in our simulations assume
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Abstract and Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results motivate modular quantum reservoir designs that align naturally with realistic hardware, such as two-dimensional quantum-chip layouts or networks of small integrated quantum systems.
quotes: These results motivate modular quantum reservoir designs that align naturally with realistic hardware, such as two-dimensional quantum-chip layouts or networks of small integrated quantum systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim; no hardware run is reported.

papers.title_in_file: Learning AC Power Flow Solutions using a Data-Dependent Variational Quantum Circuit
papers.what_it_is: A short Purdue paper that trains a data-embedded variational quantum circuit to predict AC power flow solutions and tests it on the IEEE 14-bus system in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that on its power system test case the VQC/QML model attained smaller prediction errors than the DNN in 17 out of 20 test instances.
quotes: the VQC/QML model attained smaller prediction errors than DNN in 17 out of 20 instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small study on one test system.

assertions.value: The authors report that the chosen DNN used 690 weights while the VQC/QML model used only 52 trainable weights.
quotes: Overall, the chosen DNN architecture used 690 weights.
resulting in only P = 52 trainable weights
assertions.certainty_reason: Parameter counts from the paper's own configuration; the DNN was chosen by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors describe the numerical tests as preliminary, run on an exact quantum simulator with a VQC of 4 qubits and matrices zero-padded to reach the dimension of 16.
quotes: Preliminary numerical tests indicate that the proposed VQC models attain enhanced prediction performance
exact quantum simulator
The VQC operated on 4 qubits with matrices zero-padded to reach the dimension of 16.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its test scope, Abstract and Section VI.
